newsitem.title: UK: United Assurance says H1 income declines.
newsitem.headline: United Assurance says H1 income declines.

text.p: Britain's United Assurance Group, formed by the merger of Refuge Group and United Friendly last year, on Thursday announced that its new equivalent premium and unit trust income in the first six months of 1997 fell 4.6 percent to 31.1 million stg.
The group said its industrial branch new business was broadly unchanged at 9.5 million stg. Ordinary branch sales declined to 15.6 million stg from 17.3 million.
Single premium life and pension business, however, reversed the trend to grow 4.5 percent to 36.8 million stg from 35.2 million.
Its unit trust and PEP sales also rose, by 8.2 percent, to 23.8 million stg.
George Mack, the group chief executive, said it was making "good progress" on restructuring the home sales force following the merger of Refuge and United Friendly.
The group had pursued its 'non-replacement of staff' policy as it saw its home service sales force number falling by 10 percent.
